subject: Post-call: Integration & observability instrumentation - next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Payton <jordan.payton@clearpath.health>, Leah Summers <leah.summers@clearpath.health>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Integration & observability instrumentation - next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — really productive call. Quick recap + proposed next steps so engineering has a clear path forward. Please reply with anything I missed.

Summary of call (very high level)
- Goal: embed LLM features into ClearPath Care Portal for note summarization and triage reranking.
- Primary constraints: PHI handling, <48ms p50 latency target for summarization endpoint on reserved traffic, and strict audit logs for every inference.

Key integration items we agreed to track:
1) SDK + Auth
   - Use Redwood JS SDK for initial PoC. Auth will be API key for PoC, with plan to move to mTLS + KMS for production.
   - We’ll provide a short example for server-side key usage and a pattern for token rotation.
2) Routing / model variants
   - Traffic will route to a small-capacity dedicated pool for now; fall back to hosted model variant if dedicated is saturated.
3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We recommended using Redwood’s structured output schema to ensure deterministic fields for downstream systems. Tool-calling will be gated behind a function-level allowlist.
4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Batch embedding uploads to our vector store ingestion API (we recommended n=256 batching). Reranker will use a fine-tuned candidate scorer using the sbert-family encoder.
5) Observability hooks (this is where Camila / Laura will help)
   - Required fields: request_id, trace_id (propagate W3C traceparent), model_variant, cache_hit (bool), token_count, backend_queue_ms, generate_ms, total_latency_ms.
   - Logging: structured JSON to your central logging endpoint; sampling for full request body at 0.1% to preserve PI concerns.
   - Dashboards: we propose a Grafana dashboard with token-cost per route, p50/p95 latency per model_variant, cache hit ratio, and error-rate per surface.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners and timelines)
- Camila: send SDK + auth example and a checklist for secure key handling (tomorrow EOD).
- ClearPath (Jordan & Leah): share firewall/IP allowlist and any ingestion throughput limits (by Mon 12/21).
- Diego: produce a draft mutual action plan and attach initial architecture diagram (attached).

Attachments: clearpath_architecture_v1.png (diagram, 410 KB)

Open questions we still need answers to:
- Do you have a preferred vector DB or will you let Redwood host embeddings for the PoC?
- Any DLP rules that prevent us from storing full user notes even in encrypted form?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the action items doc and a calendar invite for a technical kickoff next week.

--
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration & observability instrumentation - next steps

Thanks Diego — this lines up with our notes. A couple quick clarifications from our security/devops side: 

1) Vector DB: We prefer pushing vectors to our managed Pinecone instance for now (we have strict residency requirements). Can Redwood point embeddings calls at an external vector store or do we need to proxy through Redwood-hosted ingestion?

2) PHI & DLP: We cannot persist verbatim free-text records to any third-party store without a signed BAA. For PoC, we can pseudonymize PII before sending, but we’d like to understand what traces/logs Redwood will retain by default.

3) IP & Firewall: our infra team will send a CIDR allowlist and requirements for TLS mutual auth on Mon. Expect that to include our internal egress proxies which will perform header scrubbing.

4) Observability: the fields you listed look good. Can you confirm the header names you expect us to return so tracing links tightly across our services and Redwood’s runtime? We prefer explicit headers rather than embedding everything in the body.

We’ll prepare a short network requirements PDF and attach it to the next reply. Also looping in our Platform engineer Jordan on the detailed questions.

—
Leah Summers
Head of Product Operations
ClearPath Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration & observability instrumentation - next steps

Hi Jordan / Leah — Camila from Redwood SE team here. I’m attaching a focused integration checklist below and an example inflight of the headers and log schema we recommend. Pasted sample code is intentionally minimal — let me know if you want a repo PR instead.

Quick answers to Leah’s questions:
- Embeddings: Redwood can either host embeddings (we’ll surface vector-store write/read endpoints) or we can push raw vectors to your Pinecone endpoint. For the PoC I recommend hosting vectors on your Pinecone instance to keep control of residency; we’ll provide a connector sample.
- Logs & traces: For distributed tracing we require propagation of W3C traceparent and our X-Redwood-Request-Id header for internal correlation. We DO NOT capture request bodies by default; only metadata (see below). If you need full bodies for debugging we can do temporary retention at a 0.1% sample as Diego noted.

Recommended headers (please forward to infra):
- X-Redwood-Request-Id: (uuid) — unique per inbound client request
- traceparent: (W3C) — for trace linkage
- X-Client-Region: us-east-1 / eu-west-1 — for routing and latency breakdowns
- X-Model-Variant: redwood-llama-7b-q4 / redwood-llama-7b-q4-sparse — used for per-variant metrics
- X-Cache-Hit: true/false — backend cache indicated
- X-Token-Count: integer — total tokens billed for the request

Suggested structured log schema (JSON fields):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-12-18T16:14:00Z",
  "request_id": "uuid-v4",
  "trace_id": "00-xxxxxxx-xxxxxxx-01",
  "model_variant": "redwood-llama-7b-q4",
  "cache_hit": false,
  "backend_queue_ms": 12,
  "generate_ms": 78,
  "total_latency_ms": 105,
  "token_count": 342
}

Note on latency breakdowns: our runtime exposes per-segment timings. We recommend surface metrics for: client-to-ingress (observed by your egress proxy), ingress-auth (Redwood), backend-queue, model-generate, and egress. We can emit these as labeled Prometheus metrics and as numeric fields on the structured logs so they show up in Grafana and your SIEM (we support Datadog/CloudWatch/Splunk).

SDK / Auth example (nodejs snippet):
// server-side only
const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-llama-7b-q4',
  input: 'Summarize note',
  headers: {
    'X-Redwood-Request-Id': req.headers['x-request-id'],
    'traceparent': req.headers['traceparent'],
  }
});

Checklist (PoC)
- [ ] Provide IP/CIDR allowlist (ClearPath)
- [ ] Confirm Pinecone write endpoint or allow Redwood connector (ClearPath + Camila)
- [ ] Implement the X-Redwood-Request-Id + traceparent propagation (ClearPath infra)
- [ ] Decide sampling % for full-body debug logs (default 0.1%)
- [ ] Schedule technical kickoff and walkthrough (30–45m)

I’ve attached a lightweight architecture diagram as requested (clearpath_architecture_v1.png) and a short PDF with firewall expectations. I’ll follow up with a repo PR that includes the Pinecone connector sample and a full Prometheus metrics manifest.

—
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
